scenario_summary: A short cellphone video circulates on a regional WhatsApp network and is picked up by a partisanship-aligned local news site claiming it shows a labor leader, Marco Ribeiro, inciting a violent confrontation at last night's downtown protest. The clip is 18 seconds long, handheld, with intermittent motion blur and two missing frames that create a brief jump cut. The published article highlights the file's timestamp and an attached location tag to argue the footage is 'fresh' evidence of escalation. Our internal checks reveal the visual content of the clip matches a longer raw recording posted three months earlier by a community TV outlet after a separate, unrelated rally. The partisan outlet did not alter faces or audio; instead they edited the file header and metadata (timestamp and GPS) and re-encoded the video to remove identifying frames, then cropped it to a tight close-up to emphasize the subject. Their goal appears to be contextual re-framing rather than pixel-level fabrication. The training challenge invites reporters to verify the Who/What/Where/When/Why, locate the original source, evaluate provenance metadata (and understand its limits), and recognize practical newsroom threats such as metadata tampering and deceptive publication workflows. The scenario also creates opportunities to practice geolocation from visual clues, question provenance claims, and defend against simple social-engineering vectors used by low-sophistication partisan actors.

ground_truth.true_motive: A partisan outlet tampered with timestamps/GPS metadata and cropped the original authentic footage to misrepresent its timing and context to inflame public sentiment.

participant_briefing.role_introduction: You are Ana Silva, a regional investigations reporter at a mid-sized independent outlet based in Porto Alegre, Brazil.
participant_briefing.scenario_trigger: Today a partisan regional news site published an article claiming an 18-second video proves that labor leader Marco Ribeiro incited violence at last night's protest. The clip is circulating rapidly on WhatsApp and social platforms. Your desk asks you to verify the clip before the newsroom runs a follow-up.
participant_briefing.media_artifact_description: Video | 18-second handheld clip showing a man identified as Marco Ribeiro speaking loudly to a crowd; camera shakes, occasional motion blur, and two brief jump cuts where frames are missing. There is ambient crowd noise and a shouted phrase in Portuguese but no clear signage in the visible frames. The file published with the article includes a recent timestamp and a GPS tag that point to last night and a downtown square.
initial_context_clues: Local protests have been ongoing intermittently for months.
Partisan outlets have previously republished citizen clips with editorial framing.
The labor leader has denied calls for violence in past statements.
participant_briefing.verification_stakes: If published unverified, the clip could escalate tensions and damage the reputation of a public figure; failing to publish could leave a misleading narrative unchallenged during a volatile period.

primary_subject_description: Marco Ribeiro — mid-40s labor organizer known regionally for leading union actions; frequently photographed at rallies and has a public social media presence. He is a polarizing local figure but not nationally prominent.

media_artifact_details.dm_summary: From the DM perspective, the video frames match an earlier longer recording posted by a community TV outlet; manipulation is limited to metadata tampering (timestamp and GPS) and re-encoding/cropping that removed contextual frames. Visual tells include two missing frames causing a jump cut, slight biometric mismatches in automated face-recognition confidence scores after re-encoding, and motion blur from low-light handheld capture.
discoverable_characteristics: biometric anomalies (face-recognition confidence drop after re-encode)
inconsistent file timestamps vs. original uploads
media_artifact_details.original_source_identifier: social_media:@raiztv — longer raw video posted 2024-06-12 (community TV channel) matching multiple frames of the clip

key_moments.description: Trainee locates the original longer video posted by a community TV account and matches at least three unique visual frames to geolocate the scene.
key_moments.implementation_notes: Embed street-level clues in peripheral frames (a distinctive mural, a bus stop, partial storefront signage) to allow matching with map/street view searches.

key_moments.description: Trainee inspects file provenance and discovers altered timestamps and GPS metadata that conflict with the original upload history.
key_moments.implementation_notes: Provide a realistic metadata view showing a recent timestamp on the circulated file and a verifiable older timestamp on the original social upload.

key_moments.description: Trainee must document the 5 Ws and present a recommendation: publish with caveats, wait for confirmation, or debunk.
key_moments.implementation_notes: Create decision pressure by simulating an editor asking for a verdict within a tight deadline.

required_character_behaviors.behavior: Requests quick verification and warns about potential legal exposure; insists on source authentication before publication.
Responds to outreach but provides only the original upload link and a brief statement; expects the newsroom to cross-check metadata themselves.
Offers an anonymous tip claiming the clip was from a months-old event but provides vague location details, prompting further geolocation work.

information_to_embed.content: Original uploaded by @raiztv on 2024-06-12; circulated file shows modified header timestamp of yesterday and a GPS tag pointing to downtown square.
A partial storefront sign visible in original frames reads 'Padaria do Sol' and appears on OpenStreetMap imagery near a known square.
A forensic tool in the exercise should flag inconsistent EXIF/timestamp fields but should not claim the footage is fabricated; tools may show conflicting confidence to teach limits.
